description: The JSON envelopes the read doors wrap the protocol in. The contents are the protocol's own.

CallState.description: GET /v1/calls/{call}/state: the whole log folded, and the seq a stream resumes from.

last_seq.description: The seq the fold reached; a stream opens after it.

live.description: True while the log is still open.

LogPage.description: One page of a log: what this reader may see, whether the log is open, and where to resume.

entries.description: The entries this reader may see, in seq order.

live.description: True while the log is still open.

next.description: The last seq the page READ, or null when it read nothing.

SessionLine.description: One call as a list draws it: which call, how far the log got, and the state's own fields.

agent.description: The agent that handled it: which, when the list spans an org.

live.description: True while the call's log is still open.

channel.description: The door it came in by, once known.

from.description: The calling number or identity, once known.

to.description: The called number or identity, once known.

caller.description: Who was on the line, once known.

started_at.description: When media came up, unix seconds.

ended_at.description: When the call ended, unix seconds.

end_reason.description: Why it ended, once it did.

score.description: How the judges answered at hang-up, cut to a row; null when nobody judged the call. Absent from a gateway that predates it.

flags.description: What a person reviewing calls should look at first. Absent from a gateway that predates it.

SessionScore.description: One call's call.score as a list draws it: how many judges held of how many answered, and why the first one that broke did.

judged.description: The judges that answered held or broken. A skipped or deferred judge answered neither and is not counted.

passed.description: False when any judge answered broken.

reason.description: The first broken judge's reason, as it wrote it; null when none broke.

SessionFlag.description: escalated: a person took part — a transfer, a supervisor taking the line, saying something, or ending the call. low_score: a judge answered broken. promise: the promises judge found the agent committing the business to something no tool call records.

SessionList.description: GET /v1/agents/{slug}/sessions and GET /v1/sessions: the calls that match, newest first, a page at a time.

calls.description: One line per call, newest first.

total.description: How many calls match the filter, every page together. Absent from a gateway that predates it.

next.description: The cursor the next page is asked with as `before`, or null on the last page. Absent from a gateway that predates it.

Insights.description: GET /v1/insights: one day of the key's world and corner at a glance, counted off the call index and never off a log.

timezone.description: The zone the day is cut in. Always UTC: an org carries no timezone.

resolved_rate.description: The share, 0..1, of the day's finished calls no person took part in; null when none finished.

median_e2e_s.description: The median e2e_latency over every agent turn of the day's calls, seconds; null when no turn measured one.

spend_eur.description: What the day's calls cost, call.summary's cost summed, euros.

sessions_total.description: Every call this world's corner ever held.

live.description: The calls whose log is still open, right now.

agents.description: One row per agent that took a call that day, busiest first.

InsightsConversations.description: How many calls started on the day, and on the day before it.

today.description: Calls started on the day counted.

yesterday.description: Calls started on the day before.

InsightsChannels.description: The day's calls by the door they came in by.

today.description: Calls it started on the day.

score.description: The share of judges that held, 0..1, averaged over the day's judged calls; null when none was judged.

InsightsBudget.description: What the org may spend in a month and what it has spent so far, both worlds together.

limit_eur.description: The operator's budget_eur quota; null is no limit.

spent_eur_month.description: What calls started this calendar month (UTC) cost, every world and corner of the org.

Judging.description: GET and PUT /v1/org/judging: whether the org's calls are judged at hang-up, and what judging one may spend on a model.

on.description: False: no judge runs at hang-up, and call.score says so; a call can still be judged later by POST /v1/evals/judge/{call}.

ceiling_eur.description: What judging one call may spend on a model, euros: the box's setting, which the org reads and does not set.

on.description: Judge the org's calls at hang-up, or do not.

ThreadLast.description: The newest thing on a contact's thread.

text.description: The words, or for a spoken call its outcome; null when nothing was said.

ThreadKind.description: in: the contact wrote it. out: the agent, or a person as the agent, did. call: a spoken call, drawn as one pill.

ThreadLine.description: One contact of an agent's inbox: every call of theirs, folded into one line.

contact.description: Who: the id the app resolved, else the number or visitor id the call came from.

name.description: The contact's name when a call recorded one.

unread.description: What arrived after the reader last marked the thread read: each message the contact wrote, and each spoken call.

calls.description: How many calls the thread is made of.

ThreadList.description: GET /v1/agents/{slug}/threads: the agent's contacts, the newest thread first.

next.description: The cursor the next page is asked with as `after`, or null on the last page.

ThreadMessage.description: One message of a thread, or one spoken call drawn as a pill.

text.description: The words; for a spoken call, its outcome.

call.description: The call it belongs to: its log is the whole of it.

duration_s.description: A spoken call's length, seconds; null while it is live.

answered.description: A spoken call's: whether it ever came up.

Thread.description: GET /v1/agents/{slug}/threads/{contact}: every call of one contact, merged, oldest first.

name.description: The contact's name when a call recorded one.

text.description: What the agent says to the contact, verbatim.

ThreadSaid.description: POST /v1/agents/{slug}/threads/{contact}/messages, the answer: the call it was said on. The turn.agent it lands as is on that call's log.

call.description: The open conversation it was said on.

AgentFact.description: One current fact memory holds, across the contacts an agent's calls taught.

id.description: The fact's id: DELETE /v1/memory/facts/{id} forgets it.

category.description: The tenant's word it was filed under.

written_at.description: When it was written, unix seconds.

AgentMemory.description: GET /v1/agents/{slug}/memory: the current facts the agent's calls taught, newest first.

next.description: The cursor the next page is asked with as `after`, or null on the last page.

WidgetSettings.description: GET and PUT /v1/agents/{slug}/widget: how the widget presents this agent, kept per org, world and agent. PUT takes the whole set.

greeting.description: The first line the widget shows before the call starts, as plain text.

accent.description: The accent colour, a CSS colour.

autostart.description: Open with the microphone asked for and the call started, without a second click.

OrgSso.description: GET and PUT /v1/org/sso: the OpenID Connect provider this org's people sign in at, and never the client secret it was wired with.

configured.description: Whether a provider is wired at all. False: every field below is its empty answer, and this org's people sign in with a password.

issuer.description: The issuer as the provider publishes it, an https URL with no trailing slash: what /.well-known/openid-configuration hangs off, and what every id_token carries as `iss`.

client_id.description: The client this gateway is at that provider. Public by design; the secret beside it is sealed under the box's vault key and no door answers with it.

domains.description: The email domains this org signs in with, folded. An address outside them is refused at the callback even when the provider vouched for it.

role.description: What an address nobody invited is seated as: a member role, or null for no auto-provisioning at all — the default, which refuses a stranger.

required.description: True: a password opens this org no longer. The way back when the provider stops answering is the operator's, never the org's.

redirect_uri.description: Where the provider sends the person back — https://<gateway>/v1/login/sso/callback — which is what an admin registers at the provider. Answered even when nothing is wired, because it is what they need before they can wire anything.

OrgSsoWanted.description: PUT /v1/org/sso, the body. The configuration is replaced whole, the client secret included: it is write-only, so a change of anything else carries it again.

issuer.description: The provider's issuer, an https URL. It is fetched before anything is kept, so a typo is a refusal with nothing written.

client_id.description: The client this gateway is at that provider.

client_secret.description: Its secret. It goes in and never comes out: the row holds a Fernet token under the box's vault key.

domains.description: The email domains this org signs in with. Folded, and without an `@` somebody pasted.

role.description: The role an address nobody invited is seated with, a seat taken for it. Left out: nobody is auto-provisioned.

required.description: Whether a password opens this org any more. Left out: it does.

OrgMail.description: GET and PUT /v1/org/mail: the SMTP account this org's letters go out through, how the last one went, and never the password it was wired with. An org that wired none sends through the box's own mail, or through nothing.

configured.description: Whether this org wired a mail account of its own. False: every field below is its empty answer, and its letters go through the box's mail, or none are sent at all.

host.description: The mail server the letters are handed to.

port.description: Its port: 587 with STARTTLS, 465 with implicit TLS, 25 for a relay on the same machine.

security.description: How the connection is protected — starttls, tls or none: starttls upgrades a plain socket, tls opens protected, none is plain and is only ever right for a relay beside the gateway.

username.description: Who signs in at that server. Empty for a relay that asks for no credentials; the password beside it is sealed under the box's vault key and no door answers with it.

from.description: The From header the letters carry, as it is written: "Pinecall <no-reply@example.com>" or a bare address.

verified_at.description: When a letter was last taken by this server. Null until one has been, because a mailbox is kept without anything being sent to find out it works.

last_error.description: What the server said the last time it refused one, host and port included and credentials never. Null when the last letter went through.

OrgMailWanted.description: PUT /v1/org/mail, the body. The account is replaced whole, the password included: it is write-only, so a change of anything else carries it again — and the standing is reset with it, since what a server said about the old password is not news about a new one.

host.description: The mail server: SES's SMTP endpoint, Postmark's, Mailgun's, or one of your own.

username.description: Who signs in there. Left out: nobody, for a relay that asks for no credentials.

password.description: Its password. It goes in and never comes out: the row holds a Fernet token under the box's vault key.

from.description: Who the letters are from. An address, or a name and an address.

BoxMail.description: GET and PUT /v1/ops/mail: the SMTP account the BOX posts its letters through — what the operator stored, or the environment's two variables — how the last one went, and never the password. An org's own account (OrgMail) still wins over both.

configured.description: Whether the box can post a letter at all, from either place. False: every field below is its empty answer.

source.description: `stored` or `environment`: where the mailbox was read from — `stored` for a row the operator wrote at PUT /v1/ops/mail, which wins; `environment` for PINECALL_SMTP_URL and PINECALL_MAIL_FROM; null with neither.

host.description: The mail server the letters are handed to.

username.description: Who signs in there; empty for a relay that asks for nobody. The password beside it is sealed under the box's vault key and no door answers with it.

from.description: The From header the letters carry.

verified_at.description: When a letter was last taken through the STORED mailbox. Null for the environment's, whose outcome is in the box's log.

last_error.description: What the server said the last time it refused one through the stored mailbox, credentials never. Null when the last letter went through.

BoxBrand.description: GET and PUT /v1/ops/brand, and `brand` on GET /.well-known/pinecall: what this box's letters and its sign-in page are called and painted with. Pinecall, its accent and no logo until the operator says.

name.description: One line, at most 60 characters: it goes into a subject.

logo_url.description: An https URL of an image, drawn 28px tall at the top of every letter where the wordmark stood; null is the name as text, and a letter that fetches nothing.

accent.description: #rrggbb, six hex digits, lower-cased: the button in every letter.

BoxBrandWanted.description: PUT /v1/ops/brand, the body. A field left out keeps what it had; an empty string goes back to the default — which for the logo is none at all, the only way to clear one.

name.description: One line, at most 60 characters; empty is Pinecall again.

accent.description: #rrggbb; empty is the default accent again.

BoxProvider.description: One box-wide identity provider as the operator reads it: whether it is usable, the client this gateway is at it, and the URI to register there. Never the secret.

configured.description: Wired, and its secret openable with this box's vault key: what GET /.well-known/pinecall carries as `google`.

client_id.description: The client this gateway is at the provider, read off the row even when it is not usable, so a page shows what was typed.

redirect_uri.description: https://<gateway>/v1/login/<provider>/callback — what the operator registers at the provider as an authorised redirect URI.

BoxSignIn.description: GET /v1/ops/signin: every provider this box can offer every org's people, wired or not, one key each. Only `google` today; a second is a key here and a row on the box.

BoxProviderWanted.description: PUT /v1/ops/signin/google, the body: the OAuth client the operator made at Google for this gateway. Replaced whole, the secret write-only; the issuer is Google's own and is not a field.

client_id.description: The web client's id, as Google's console shows it.

client_secret.description: Goes in and never comes out: the row holds a Fernet token under the box's vault key.

MailSent.description: POST /v1/org/mail/test: one letter, waited for — the only door of this runtime that waits for a mail server, because it is the one a person is watching.

sent.description: Whether the mail server took it.

error.description: What it said when it did not, host and port included and credentials never. Null when it took it.

SsoOrg.description: One org a sign-in page may send somebody to, named — and nothing about whether anybody answers to the address that asked.

slug.description: Its slug, which is what GET /v1/login/sso?org= takes.

name.description: What to call it on the page.

SsoDiscovery.description: POST /v1/login/sso/discover: the orgs whose domains match an address's and that wired a provider. Empty is the answer for a domain nobody wired, and for a box that keeps no provider at all.

HeldAgent.description: One agent, as somebody choosing which to open needs to see it: its name and its channels.

slug.description: The agent's slug, which every other door takes.

channels.description: The doors it answers on, sorted.

holder.description: Whose copy this is: the member holding it in their sandbox, by id and by the address a person reads. Absent for the ORG's — what a machine key holds, which is production, and which in a sandbox is the team's shared one. A key that opens `team` is shown every member's; every other key is shown its own and the org's.

AgentList.description: GET /v1/agents: every agent this fleet is holding right now, as the front page lists them.

agents.description: One row per agent, in the order their sockets claimed them.

LineHolder.description: One corner of a world holding an agent: the member whose it is, named so a person can read it.

holder.description: The member id whose corner it is, or null for the org's own — a machine key names nobody.

name.description: Who that member is, for a person reading a terminal. Null for the org's own corner.

TheLine.description: GET /v1/agents/{slug}/line: whose terminal a call that RINGS at this agent's doors lands in. An org shares one sandbox number, so it rings in one place and which one is claimed.

agent.description: The agent whose ringing doors these are.

env.description: The world. Production has one corner and always holds its own line.

held.description: Whether any corner is answering the ring at all. False means a call at the number reaches nobody.

holding.description: The corner answering it. Absent when nobody is.

yours.description: Whether the line is this key's corner, so a terminal knows to say 'you' rather than a name.

waiting.description: Every other corner holding this agent that could claim it, newest claim first.

calling.description: The numbers whose calls reach the ASKING corner directly, whoever holds the line. A developer says which phone is theirs once and every call they make lands in their own corner.

KnowledgePush.description: PUT /v1/knowledge/{base}, the body: the tenant's folder as of now, sent whole. The base is replaced, never merged.

files.description: Every file of the base, path and text. A file not in the list is gone from the base.

GoldenQuestion.description: One question of a base's golden: what somebody asks, and the chunk that should answer it. A chunk answers when its file and heading path start with `expects`, so naming a file alone accepts any chunk of it and naming a heading accepts that section.

asks.description: The question, in the words a caller would use.

expects.description: The chunk that should win, as its heading path: 'tarifas.md › Tarifas › Revisión', or 'tarifas.md' for any chunk of the file.

KnowledgeGolden.description: POST /v1/knowledge/{base}/eval, the body: the questions a base is held to. A golden is fixed and the index is the variable; a question is never softened so a change can pass.

k.description: How many chunks a search may return, as the agent asks for them. Absent: the base's own default.

GoldenMiss.description: One question whose expected chunk was not among the k returned, and what came back instead.

expects.description: The chunk that should have won.

found.description: The heading paths that came back, best first.

KnowledgeScore.description: POST /v1/knowledge/{base}/eval, the answer: how the index did on its own golden. Both figures are computed by code, with no model, so two runs of the same golden over the same base answer the same numbers.

model.description: The embedder the base was pushed with; two scores are comparable only under one model.

k.description: How many chunks a search returned for each.

recall_at_k.description: The share of questions whose expected chunk was among the k returned, 0 to 1. The figure that matters: a chunk the model never sees cannot be used, whatever its rank.

ndcg_at_10.description: How high the expected chunk ranked, discounted logarithmically and normalised, 0 to 1. Two indexes that both find a passage are not equal if one puts it first and the other seventh.

took_ms.description: How long the whole golden took, in milliseconds.

misses.description: Every question the base missed, so the person who wrote the documents can read what came back instead.

KnowledgePushed.description: PUT /v1/knowledge/{base}, the answer: which base, how many chunks it became, and how long that took.

base.description: The base's name, as the path named it.

chunks.description: How many chunks the files were cut into and embedded.

took_ms.description: How long the push took, chunking and embedding included, in milliseconds.

KnowledgeBase.description: One knowledge base as the list draws it: its name, its size, and when it was last pushed.

model.description: The embedder that wrote its vectors. Two bases are only comparable, and a base is only searchable, under the model it was pushed with.

pushed_at.description: When it was last pushed, unix seconds.

KnowledgeList.description: GET /v1/knowledge: every base this org has pushed.

bases.description: One row per base, by name.

ContactFact.description: One fact of a contact's history: a MemoryFact with the two dates that bound it. A fact is never deleted, only superseded, so the history keeps every version.

id.description: The fact's id in the memory store.

text.description: The fact itself, as one sentence.

category.description: The tenant's own word for what kind of fact this is, from its memory.remember list.

source.description: The call this fact was extracted from, when known.

valid_from.description: When the fact was written, unix seconds.

invalidated_at.description: When a later call superseded or withdrew it, unix seconds; null while it is current.

ContactMemory.description: GET /v1/contacts/{contact}/memory: everything memory ever kept about one contact, current facts first.

facts.description: Every version of every fact, current first, then the superseded ones, newest first.

Forgotten.description: DELETE /v1/contacts/{contact}/memory, the answer: how many facts the right to be forgotten erased.

forgotten.description: How many facts were erased, every version counted.

MemoryQuestion.description: One question of a memory golden: what memory holds about the contact who asks it, the words they just said, and the fact or facts that should come back. The facts are the question's own, so a golden needs no contact in any table.

holds.description: Every fact memory holds about this question's contact, in the words a fact is written in. More facts than a turn asks for is what makes a question discriminate: with fewer, everything comes back and recall@k is 1.00 whatever the ranking did.

asks.description: What the caller just said, in their own words.

expects.description: The fact or facts that should come back. One answers when what came back CONTAINS it, folded for case and accents, so a golden names the substance and never the wording.

MemoryGolden.description: POST /v1/contacts/memory/eval, the body: the questions memory is held to. Each question brings its own facts, which are written to a scratch contact of this org, asked, and deleted. A golden is fixed and the ranking is the variable; a question is never softened so a change can pass.

k.description: How many facts a recall may return, as a turn asks for them. Absent: the runtime's own default.

MemoryMiss.description: One question memory did not answer whole: what it wanted and did not get, and what came back instead. GoldenMiss is the knowledge base's and names the one chunk that should have won; a memory question may expect several facts and miss some of them.

missing.description: Every fact the question expected and did not get back.

found.description: The facts that came back, best first.

MemoryScore.description: POST /v1/contacts/memory/eval, the answer: how memory ranked the facts its own golden asked for. Both figures are computed by code, with no model in the loop, so two runs of one golden answer the same numbers.

model.description: The embedder that wrote the vectors on both sides of the recall; two scores are comparable only under one model.

k.description: How many facts a recall returned for each.

recall_at_k.description: The share of the facts asked for that came back at all, 0 to 1. The figure that matters: a fact the model never sees cannot be used, whatever its rank.

ndcg_at_10.description: How high those facts ranked, discounted logarithmically and normalised, 0 to 1. A turn asks for six facts, so a question whose contact holds few of them is answered whole by any ranking and this is the figure that still moves.

took_ms.description: How long the whole golden took, the writes and the deletes included, in milliseconds.

misses.description: Every question memory did not answer whole, so the person who wrote the golden can read what came back instead.

ExtractionExpected.description: What must come of one call's hang-up: each field is one of the four ways a hang-up costs a business. Nothing here compares one sentence to another — a category is the class's own word, a value is a literal the caller said out loud, and a supersession is an id — because two ways of writing one fact are one fact.

writes.description: Every category named got at least one fact. The class's own memory.remember words.

never.description: No fact was written under any of these. The class's own memory.forget words.

never_says.description: The sharper half of never: no fact CARRIES one of these values, under whatever category. A card number the caller read out is what this exists for, and it matches on the folded words and on the bare digits alike.

invalidates.description: Every held fact named here was superseded, and — the mirror, which catches the model that supersedes whatever it touches — no other held fact was. A fact is named by its own text.

ExtractionGolden.description: One call written down and what memory must make of it: the write side of the table, judged by code. The read side is MemoryGolden and neither answers for the other — a call may extract the perfect fact and never see it again, because six is what a turn is handed and the seventh is cut.

name.description: What this case is called, in a report and in --grep. A file that names none is called after its own basename.

said.description: The call as it happened, one [who, what] per line: `caller` is the person and anything else is the agent. Both speakers, because nothing here is re-run — a golden about extraction is a conversation ALREADY held, handed to the hang-up's one model call.

holds.description: What memory already holds about this contact, in the words a fact is written in. They are shown to the model with ids, and an expect.invalidates names one of them by its own text.

plants.description: Sentences somebody tried to get into memory. Planting one IS the assertion: admission must refuse every one of them, whatever the model did with the conversation itself.

ExtractionCases.description: POST /v1/agents/{slug}/memory/extraction, the body: the goldens whole, as the tenant wrote them down. Each costs ONE model call — the very one a hang-up makes — run on the org's own model and keys against the class the caller is holding.

cases.description: The cases, in any order. They are run one at a time: a suite is run when somebody changed the prompt or the model, never on a caller's clock.

ExtractionBroke.description: One thing that did not hold about a case: which of the questions, and the evidence in a sentence a person can act on.

check.description: The field that did not hold: writes, never, never_says, invalidates or plants.

detail.description: What was found instead, naming the fact or the category, so the person who wrote the golden reads why.

ExtractionJudged.description: One case, run: what memory would have kept, what admission refused, and what did not hold.

held.description: Whether every check passed. False when broke carries anything.

wrote.description: What memory would have kept, one op per line: the verb, the category and the sentence.

refused.description: What the model asked for and admission dropped before the table. A planted sentence belongs here.

broke.description: Everything that did not hold. Empty when held is true.

ExtractionRun.description: POST /v1/agents/{slug}/memory/extraction, the answer: which model answered, how many cases held, and every one of them. A verb prints this and a pipeline exits on it.

agent.description: The slug the cases were judged against, whose declaration is the vocabulary they may name.

model.description: The model that made each extraction, as vendor/model. Two runs are comparable only under one model.

held.description: How many of them held. A verb exits 0 when this equals cases and 1 otherwise.

took_ms.description: How long the whole run took, every model call included, in milliseconds.

results.description: Every case, in the order it was run.

LookupRequest.description: POST /v1/calls/{call}/lookup, the body: which platform tool to run for this turn, and what to run it with. Worker-only; the gateway runs it against its own stores and writes memory.ops or docs.sources on the call's log itself.

input.description: The tool's arguments, whole and unread: the wire carries the object and never looks inside it, because what recall and search take is the runtime's shape and is documented in the runtime's own docs, not here.

speech_id.description: The turn's speech_id, so the entries the lookup writes join the turn's metrics.

LookupResult.description: POST /v1/calls/{call}/lookup, the answer: what the tool found, and how long finding it took. The output is JSON-encoded into a tool_result block, which is where everything from outside the conversation goes and the only place it goes.

output.description: What the tool answered, whole and unread: the wire carries the object and never looks inside it, because the shapes recall and search answer in are the runtime's and are documented in the runtime's own docs, not here.

took_ms.description: How long the lookup took, the search and the embedding included, in milliseconds. The worker's budget is 250.

Remembered.description: POST /v1/calls/{call}/remember, the answer: what the call taught about the contact, counted. Worker-only; the body is empty, the gateway reads the turns off its own log and writes memory.ops itself.

ops.description: How many memory operations the call produced: adds, updates and invalidations together.

took_ms.description: How long remembering took, the one model call included, in milliseconds.

Dialled.description: POST /v1/agents/{slug}/dial, the answer: the call a dial became, accepted before the far end has heard anything ring.

call.description: The id of the call this became; its log opens with call.dialing.

agent.description: The agent that will answer on it.

from.description: The org's own number the call shows as coming from, E.164.

DialGuards.description: GET /v1/carrier/outbound, the guards: what this org may dial and how often.

dial_anywhere.description: False, the default, means a destination must already have called or written to this org — a call back goes back to somebody. Only an operator lifts it.

per_minute.description: How many outbound calls this org may place in a minute.

max_duration_s.description: How long one outbound call may run before the platform ends it.

CarrierOutbound.description: GET /v1/carrier/outbound, the answer: whether this org can place a call yet, and what is missing.

ready.description: Whether a call placed right now would reach the carrier.

kind.description: The carrier this org brought, `twilio` or `sip`; null when it brought none.

from_numbers.description: The org's own numbers a call may be shown as coming from, E.164.

steps_missing.description: One sentence per thing still to do before a call can be placed, empty when nothing is.

OutboundProvisioned.description: POST /v1/carrier/outbound, the answer: the plan, and whether it was carried out.

steps.description: Each step of the provisioning, in order, saying what was found standing and what was made — the same shape POST /v1/numbers answers with.

dry_run.description: True when this was the plan and nothing was written.

ready.description: Whether the org can place a call now.

trunk.description: The SFU's own id for the org's outbound trunk, once there is one.

address.description: Where the box sends a call it places through this trunk.

TuningBody.description: An agent's tuning: what the org set over what the app declared, per world and per corner. Every field is optional; one left out is not set, and what the app declared — or the runtime's own default — stands for it.

voice.description: The voice that speaks: a curated name, or the vendor's own id when `tts` names the vendor.

tts.description: The vendor that speaks, `cartesia` or `cartesia/sonic-3`: a bare vendor keeps its own default model.

tts_model.description: The model the voice speaks with; wins over a model named in `tts`.

stt.description: The ears: `vendor/model`, a vendor alone, or a model alone on whichever vendor is in use.

llm.description: The model that decides: `vendor/model`, a vendor alone, or a model alone on whichever vendor is in use.

knowledge.description: The knowledge bases the agent answers from, each with how its chunks reach the model. The first is the one a turn retrieves from today.

TuningRow.description: One kept version of an agent's tuning: whose corner, which version, who set it and when, and what it says.

holder.description: Whose corner: a member's id in the sandbox, or the empty string for the org's own.

version.description: This corner's version number, from 1, never reused.

author.description: Who set it: the member, else the key's id; `migration` for a row the schema itself wrote.

note.description: Why, in the author's words, when they said.

set_at.description: When it was set, unix seconds.

TuningAnswer.description: GET /v1/agents/{slug}/settings: the agent's tuning as this key sees it — its own corner's, the team's and production's, each corner's own newest row, or null when that corner set nothing.

yours.description: Your own sandbox corner's newest; null when you set nothing there, or the key holds no corner of its own.

team.description: The org's own corner of the key's world.

production.description: The org's own corner of production.

TuningPut.description: PUT /v1/agents/{slug}/settings, the body: the whole set, the version it was read at, why, and whose corner.

if_version.description: The corner's version this set was written over; 409 when the corner has moved on since. Null skips the check.

team.description: Write the org's own corner of the sandbox rather than your own.

TuningHistory.description: GET /v1/agents/{slug}/settings/history: one corner's versions, newest first.

holder.description: Whose corner the rows are: a member's id, or the empty string for the org's own.

rows.description: Every version this corner kept, newest first.

TuningDiff.description: GET /v1/agents/{slug}/settings/diff: what this key's corner reads against another corner's newest, and which fields differ.

ours.description: What the key's corner reads: its own newest, else the org's own.

changed.description: The fields whose values differ, by name.

Rollback.description: POST /v1/agents/{slug}/settings/rollback, the body: which version to bring back. It comes back as a NEW version; nothing is deleted.

team.description: In the org's own corner of the sandbox rather than your own.

Promoted.description: POST /v1/agents/{slug}/settings/promote and POST /v1/lexicon/promote, the answer: the version the promotion wrote, and where.

holder.description: The corner written: always the org's own, the empty string.

version.description: The new version in that corner.

run.description: The id of the eval run that gated a promotion to production, readable at GET /v1/evals/runs/{id}; null when no goldens ran.

LexiconBody.description: The org's lexicon: how the voice says the words it would get wrong, and the words the ears must know. Shared by every agent of the org, laid over each one's own says and hears.

said.description: How each word is said: a brand, a surname, an acronym.

heard.description: The words the ears must know, given to the STT as keyterms.

LexiconRow.description: One kept version of the org's lexicon.

holder.description: Whose corner: a member's id in the sandbox, or the empty string for the org's own.

version.description: This corner's version number, from 1, never reused.

author.description: Who set it: the member, else the key's id.

set_at.description: When it was set, unix seconds.

LexiconAnswer.description: GET /v1/lexicon: the org's words as this key sees them — its own corner's, the team's and production's, each corner's own newest, or null.

yours.description: Your own sandbox corner's newest, or null.

team.description: The org's own corner of the key's world.

production.description: The org's own corner of production.

LexiconPut.description: PUT /v1/lexicon, the body: the whole lexicon, the version it was read at, why, and whose corner.

if_version.description: The corner's version this was written over; 409 when it moved on. Null skips the check.

team.description: Write the org's own corner of the sandbox rather than your own.

LexiconHistory.description: GET /v1/lexicon/history: one corner's versions, newest first.

rows.description: Every version this corner kept, newest first.

CallTuning.description: GET /v1/calls/{call}/settings: the exact tuning and lexicon a call was built on, by the versions its head row recorded.

config_version.description: The tuning version the call ran on; null when its corner had set nothing.

lexicon_version.description: The lexicon version the call ran on; null when its corner had set nothing.

KnowledgePromote.description: POST /v1/knowledge/{base}/promote, the body: the golden the base is held to before it reaches production, when there is one.

KnowledgePromoted.description: POST /v1/knowledge/{base}/promote, the answer: the base as production now holds it, and the two recalls that gated it when a golden was sent.

chunks.description: How many chunks production holds now.

recall_before.description: recall@k of the golden over production's base before the copy; null when production had none, or no golden was sent.

recall_after.description: recall@k of the golden over the base promoted; null when no golden was sent.

KnowledgeUses.description: GET /v1/knowledge/attached: which agents read each base, off every agent's newest settings in this world.

bases.description: One row per base any agent reads.

KnowledgeUse.description: One base and the agents whose settings attach it.

agents.description: The agents that read it, by slug.
